label: Final-six campaign (Trials 5-7 continuation, mid-campaign concurrency amendment 3 to 6)
limitations: The final screening campaign is complete: incremental build meets the reported 5-of-6 criterion at 6/6 with three attempts per provider; four other finalists stopped after passing made 5/6 unreachable. Effective histories use the documented historical coverage repairs where applicable.

Early stopping applies per the user-reported acceptance rule: once a package can no longer reach 5 failures out of 6 scored attempts, its remaining authorized slots are not dispatched. Four of five packages stopped one or more attempts short of a complete, balanced three-Claude/three-Codex six-run set for exactly this reason -- not infrastructure or budget exhaustion.

Concurrency was raised from 3 to 6 mid-campaign by explicit user authorization. The original three-slot scheduler was paused (not killed) so its three in-flight attempts could complete undisturbed; a separate expansion controller adopted those three and launched three more. The superseded scheduler was terminated only after all six attempts were scored and it had been confirmed to still be in a paused state, never resumed.

The two packages carrying a supplemental grading policy (temporal-capacity-repair, snapshot-recovery-repair) were graded against `final-six-coverage-v1` in addition to the base service/checker grade; effectiveReward is the conjunction of the recorded grade and the supplemental result. The other three packages have no supplemental policy; their effective and recorded rewards are identical.

CLI dollar estimates (Claude runs only) are not subscription charges; billingMode was subscription-only with maxMicroUsd 0 and no paid API fallback. Requested model/effort are not independent backend attestations.
Solvers were given only the original public task inputs -- no access to any prior trial, analysis, the audit, or this campaign's operator handoff.
sourceProvenance: Reused, byte-for-byte, the isolated runtime built and independently verified for the first round-two campaign. No new runtime was built for this campaign.

concurrencyAmendment.originalSchedulerHandling: Paused via SIGSTOP before its three in-flight children were adopted by a separate expansion controller (which independently confirmed the pause via `ps -o stat`, and would have resumed it automatically had adoption failed). Never resumed. Terminated via SIGKILL only after all six attempts were scored and FINAL.json reported zero errors; SIGTERM was attempted first and had no effect, which is expected for a stopped process.
